subject: Projection of latitude and longitude to XY cartesian system

messages.author: 77adf69b9d056987
messages.subject: Projection of latitude and longitude to XY cartesian system
parts:
Dear all,

Good morning. I'm working on a set of traps. I have the latitude and longitude where each trap is located. But I understand that I must transform and project latitude and longitude to a system of Cartesian XY coordinates on a scale of meters or kms. I have latitude and longitude in two columns for each trap. 

What package R do you recommend to me to do the transformation (projection). 

I understand that I cannot use oSCR latitude and longitude directly to define the location of the traps. 

Please, correct me if I'm wrong. 

Greetings, 

Victor

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Projection of latitude and longitude to XY cartesian system
parts:
Hi Victor, this is a general problem that goes far beyond oSCR.  You cannot measure Euclidean distance with latitude and longitude.

Depending on where the study was located, you could choose one of the 60 longitudinal UTM zones on which to project the coordinates.  The following link provides some guidance in R:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/18639967/converting-latitude-and-longitude-points-to-utm

And here is a map of the longitudinal zones to choose.  I believe R should be able to handle the appropriate latitudinal zone.
http://www.dmap.co.uk/utmworld.htm

messages.subject: Re: Projection of latitude and longitude to XY cartesian system
parts:
Hi Victor,
Another example, similar to the one Daniel shared, would be:

gps <- read.csv('gpsfile.csv', header = T)
xy <- cbind(gps$x,gps$y)
a<-project(xy, "+proj=utm +zone=11 ellps=WGS84")  # zone will vary
gps$x<-round(a[,1])
gps$y<-a[,2]
head(gps)

Best,
Esther
